topic_development_chronological.topic: Decision: defer resampling/chunking until after ASVspoof integration
topic_development_chronological.development: User asked whether the recommended fixes could be done after integrating ASVspoof 2019 LA instead of before. Answer given: yes, and actually preferable — avoids doing the unification work twice, and ASVspoof's native 16kHz rate would confirm (not just guess) the correct target sample rate. Caveat stated: don't run build_metadata.py or feature extraction on raw data in the meantime, since the confound would still be live until fixed.

A 7-step plan was given: download LA specifically (not PA), extract preserving official train/dev/eval structure (not flattened like the other two sources, to preserve speaker-disjointness), parse protocol files into organize_asvspoof.py without physically copying audio (reference original paths instead), extend the audit script, do the deferred unification work with all three sources visible, rebuild metadata with source/speaker_id/system_id/subset columns, and decide the cross-dataset split strategy.

User flagged limited disk space before downloading ASVspoof. Guidance given: check free space, download only train+dev (skip eval) if possible, delete archives immediately after extraction, keep FLAC rather than converting to WAV (3-5x size difference), reference files in place rather than copying into organized folders, resample on-the-fly at feature-extraction time rather than persisting full resampled copies. User later reported actual free space: 29.06GB free of 445.65GB total — assessed as sufficient headroom (peak extraction usage ~7-8GB, well under half of free space) to proceed safely with train+dev.

topic_development_chronological.topic: Download turned out to be the full LA+PA package, not separable
topic_development_chronological.development: User could not selectively download train+dev only — the source provided a combined package containing evaluation_plan PDF, an Interspeech paper PDF, a LICENSE_text, README, and two zipped folders: LA (7.46GB compressed) and PA (17.25GB compressed). Guidance given: extract LA only (matches voice-cloning threat model — TTS/voice-conversion attacks); do not extract PA at all (replay-attack data, a different threat category, irrelevant to this project) and delete it entirely to reclaim ~17GB.

User hit a persistent 'unspecified error' trying to delete PA. Multiple rounds of troubleshooting were provided (close locking programs, check Task Manager, delete via Command Prompt/PowerShell, clear file attributes, take ownership via takeown/icacls, check path length, Safe Mode, chkdsk). Root cause eventually surfaced: user was not deleting an extracted file at all — they were trying to delete an entry from *inside* the still-compressed zip archive via Explorer's built-in zip viewer, which is flaky for large archives. Correct fix given: extract only the LA folder from within the zip to a real location on disk, verify it, then delete the *entire original zip* (a normal file operation, not an in-archive deletion) — never touching PA directly. User confirmed this worked: extracted LA successfully, deleted the original combined zip afterward.

Script parses ASVspoof 2019 LA protocol files (format: speaker_id, utterance_id, -, system_id, key) for train/dev/eval subsets, maps key='bonafide'/other to bonafide/spoof labels, and writes a manifest CSV (asvspoof2019_la_manifest.csv) with columns: source, subset, speaker_id, utterance_id, system_id, label, audio_path — referencing original FLAC file locations, never copying audio. This was the concrete implementation of the 'reference in place' disk-space strategy agreed earlier.

A standalone audit_asvspoof.py was written (reads manifest, checks each file via soundfile for corruption/duration/sample rate, prints a summary table) as a lower-risk alternative to blindly editing the user's existing audit_datasets.py sight-unseen. Results: 0 corrupt files across all six subset/label groups (train/dev/eval x bonafide/spoof); sample rate uniformly 16000Hz everywhere (no confound, unlike gary_stafford); mean durations ~3.1-3.5s (short-form, matching gary_stafford's scale, not DEEP-VOICE's). Two findings flagged from these numbers: (1) eval subset came along 'for free' since it wasn't separable from train+dev in the download — recommended treating it as the field-standard held-out test set (train on train, tune on dev, report final metrics on eval only, never fold eval into training); (2) roughly 8.8:1 spoof:bonafide imbalance in every subset, by design in the ASVspoof protocol (many attack systems, one bonafide class), requiring class-weighting at training time rather than being treated as a data defect.

topic_development_chronological.topic: User provided the actual original audit_datasets.py source
topic_development_chronological.development: User shared their real script (pandas-based, iterates deep_voice/gary_stafford folders, writes per-file rows including a 'channels' column, groups by source+label for the printed summary — notably NOT a pre-aggregated summary CSV as an earlier assistant guess had assumed). This corrected an earlier proposed 'unified audit extension' script that had wrongly assumed a summary-row schema. A corrected version was written that extends the real per-file script: adds a 'subset' column, reads ASVspoof via its manifest instead of a folder scan, normalizes ASVspoof's bonafide/spoof labels to real/fake for consistency with this file's existing convention (noted explicitly as a report-only normalization — master_metadata.csv keeps bonafide/spoof as the forward-looking standard). Run successfully; results matched the standalone ASVspoof audit exactly, now unified into one audit_report.csv.

Before writing any chunking code, the user asked to decide the strategy first. Five decisions were laid out with reasoning: window length (4 seconds, matching ASVspoof literature convention and close to gary_stafford's per-class means), overlap (non-overlapping, to avoid near-duplicate correlated samples inflating DEEP-VOICE's eventual test-set size), silence handling (RMS-energy-based VAD trim, not a heavier trained VAD like webrtcvad — justified via feasibility/complexity tradeoff, not because a heavier VAD would be wrong, but because the problem here is coarse silence-vs-content, not precise speech-boundary detection, and adding a C-extension dependency for one small dataset wasn't worth it), trailing remainder handling (discard if under 2s, keep if 2s+), and order of operations (resample first, then chunk, so window boundaries are exact sample counts). User explicitly asked why a heavier VAD wasn't preferable — answered with the specific tradeoff (webrtcvad's precision doesn't matter for a windowing-only downstream use, adds install friction, and the recommendation was framed as 'start simple, upgrade only if RMS-energy demonstrably fails' rather than a flat dismissal). User then confirmed both decisions (4s non-overlapping windows, RMS-energy threshold) and asked a clarifying architecture question: would the same script also resample gary_stafford? Answered no — two separate scripts, since DEEP-VOICE needs three operations (resample+trim+chunk) while gary_stafford's real class needs only one (resample); conflating them would produce an awkward branching script rather than two clean, independently-rerunnable ones.

Script: librosa.load with sr=16000 (resample), librosa.effects.trim with top_db=30 (VAD-style silence trim), non-overlapping 4-second windowing with an RMS-energy check per window (discard mostly-silent windows), remainder handling (keep only if >=2s and not silent), writes chunks to data/interim/deep_voice_chunks/{real,fake}/ plus a manifest with parent_file/chunk_index/label/chunk_path columns for traceability. Run result: 7,237 total chunks — 836 real from 8 source files, 6,401 fake from 56 source files.

topic_development_chronological.topic: DEEP-VOICE evaluation methodology flagged and saved to memory
topic_development_chronological.development: The post-chunking imbalance (836:6401, ~7.7:1) was flagged as now living inside the TEST set specifically (since DEEP-VOICE's entire role is as held-out generalization data, not training data) — meaning pooled accuracy on DEEP-VOICE would be misleading (a naive always-predict-fake model would score ~88%). Recommendation: report per-class metrics (recall on real, recall on fake, or balanced accuracy), and report both chunk-level AND file-level (8 real files / 56 fake files) results, since chunks from the same source file are correlated, not independent samples — a single anomalous source file could account for 100+ 'wrong' chunks that are really one correlated failure. User explicitly requested this be saved to persistent memory; it was added as memory edit #2.

Script uses librosa.load(..., sr=16000) to resample only gary_stafford's real class (44100Hz -> 16000Hz), writes to data/interim/gary_stafford_real_16k/, with a manifest tracking original_file, resampled_path, sample rates, duration. A known minor inaccuracy was flagged and left as-is by mutual agreement: the manifest's 'original_sample_rate' field actually captures the post-resample target rate due to how librosa.load's return value works, not a true original-rate readout — acceptable here since the true original rate (44100) was already independently confirmed via the audit, so no information is actually lost, just a field label that doesn't do what its name implies. Run result: 933 files resampled, 0 failed, matching the audit's expected count exactly.

topic_development_chronological.topic: build_metadata.py written and run — the core Phase 6 deliverable
topic_development_chronological.development: Unifies all three sources into master_metadata.csv with schema: audio_path, source, label (bonafide/spoof), split, speaker_id, system_id, parent_file, chunk_index, sample_rate, duration_sec. Split logic implemented as previously agreed: ASVspoof's official subset passthrough (train->train, dev->val, eval->test); gary_stafford stratified train_test_split by label (70/15/15, fixed random_state=42, done in two sequential sklearn splits to get three-way stratification); DEEP-VOICE hardcoded entirely to split='test'. Gary_stafford's fake class (untouched raw files, already 16000Hz) was read directly via a folder scan since it never went through a resampling script and has no separate manifest. Run result: 130,564 total rows (asvspoof2019_la: 121,461; deep_voice: 7,237; gary_stafford: 1,866 with a 1,306/280/280 train/val/test stratified split). Final composition confirmed via printed breakdown table: train 3,233 bonafide / 23,453 spoof (~7.3:1), val 2,688/22,436 (~8.3:1), test 8,331/70,423 (~8.5:1, includes all of DEEP-VOICE and ASVspoof eval).

Train/val ratios were noted as consistent with each other (~7.3:1 vs ~8.3:1, both ASVspoof-dominated), meaning val should be a fair proxy for train-time tuning; gary_stafford's stratified split landed almost exactly on the intended 70/15/15 ratio, confirming the split code worked correctly.

User asked for a final review of any remaining preprocessing gaps before committing to feature extraction. Two real gaps were identified (as opposed to items already fully addressed, which were listed and confirmed complete): (1) mono/channel consistency had never been explicitly confirmed for gary_stafford's untouched fake class or for ASVspoof (only forced for deep_voice and gary_stafford's real class, both of which went through mono=True resampling scripts); (2) no validation that all master_metadata.csv audio_path entries actually resolve to real files on disk, which matters especially for ASVspoof since those paths point outside the organized data/raw structure to wherever the user extracted LA/.

topic_development_chronological.topic: validate_metadata.py written and run — first version
topic_development_chronological.development: Combined script: (a) channel consistency check reading audit_report.csv, grouped by source only; (b) path existence check plus ASVspoof duration backfill (since asvspoof2019_la_manifest.csv never tracked duration) on master_metadata.csv, with the updated file written back out in place. User explicitly requested loudness/amplitude normalization be deferred to feature extraction rather than handled now; this was saved to persistent memory as memory edit #3. Run result: path check and duration backfill succeeded cleanly (130,564 rows checked, 121,461 ASVspoof durations filled, 0 missing paths) — but channel check raised warnings: deep_voice showed {'2': 64} (all stereo) and gary_stafford showed a mixed {{'2': 933, '1': 933}} split, while asvspoof2019_la was clean mono.

topic_development_chronological.topic: Correctly diagnosing the channel warning as likely a false alarm from a flawed check, not necessarily real data problems
topic_development_chronological.development: Rather than treating the warning at face value, the check itself was scrutinized: audit_report.csv reflects the ORIGINAL raw files (pre-chunking, pre-resampling), not the actual files referenced by master_metadata.csv's audio_path column, which for deep_voice and gary_stafford's real class point at data/interim/ outputs from scripts that already forced mono=True during processing. Additionally, the source-only grouping in the first validate_metadata.py masked a likely per-label difference within gary_stafford (raw real files vs. raw fake files could differ in channel count, bundled together misleadingly as one 'mixed' result). A corrected, more targeted script (check_actual_channels.py) was written to check the actual files in master_metadata.csv, grouped by source AND label. Run result confirmed the hypothesis exactly: all six source/label groups (asvspoof2019_la/bonafide, asvspoof2019_la/spoof, deep_voice/bonafide, deep_voice/spoof, gary_stafford/bonafide, gary_stafford/spoof) came back uniformly mono. The earlier warning was fully explained as stale-data artifact, not a real defect — no fix was needed.
